## YOUR ASSIGNMENT: Injective elimination and Buchberger normalization for idempotent semiring congruences

### Core formal target

Work in a commutative idempotent semiring `S` and finite variable types `σ, τ`. Let `ι : τ ↪ σ` be an embedding. The first decisive theorem is the injective-variable analogue of elimination for finitely generated congruences on multivariate polynomial semirings.

A precise Lean target should be organized around the existing congruence API for `MvPolynomial` and the renaming map `MvPolynomial.rename`. If the current catalog theorem `elimination_fg` is stated using a subsemiring / range formulation, mirror that statement as closely as possible and prove the injective version by reducing to the range-subtype case.

Use a theorem of the following shape:

```lean
theorem elimination_fg_of_embedding
    {S σ τ : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [IsIdempotentElem S (+)]
    [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] [Fintype τ] [DecidableEq τ]
    (ι : τ ↪ σ)
    (C : Con (MvPolynomial σ S)) :
    C.FinitelyGenerated →
    (C.comap (MvPolynomial.rename ι)).FinitelyGenerated
```

If the existing API uses `SetLike`/`RingCon`-style notation or a custom congruence structure, adapt the signature, but keep the mathematical content exactly this: finite generation descends along injective renaming.

A stronger and often more useful formulation is the range-intersection form:

```lean
def renameSubsemiring (ι : τ ↪ σ) : Subsemiring (MvPolynomial σ S) := ...

theorem fg_intersection_range_of_embedding
    {S σ τ : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [IsIdempotentElem S (+)]
    [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] [Fintype τ] [DecidableEq τ]
    (ι : τ ↪ σ)
    (C : Con (MvPolynomial σ S)) :
    C.FinitelyGenerated →
    (C.restrict (renameSubsemiring (S := S) ι)).FinitelyGenerated
```

and then derive `elimination_fg_of_embedding` via the semiring equivalence
between `MvPolynomial τ S` and the image/range subsemiring cut out by `ι`.

The second target is to build the normalization infrastructure for finite pair sets. Start with definitions that are weak enough to formalize now, but strong enough to support completion.

### Definitions to introduce

Define a monomial-support signature for a polynomial pair `(f,g)`; avoid coefficient-sensitive leading terms initially, since idempotent addition makes support data the correct invariant.

Suggested Lean definitions:

```lean
def polySupportFinset
    {σ S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [DecidableEq σ]
    (f : MvPolynomial σ S) : Finset (σ →₀ ℕ) := ...

def pairSignature
    {σ S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [DecidableEq σ]
    (p : MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S) :
    Finset (σ →₀ ℕ) :=
  polySupportFinset p.1 ∪ polySupportFinset p.2
```

Then define a reduction relation modulo a finite set `G : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S)`. Keep the first version syntactic and support-decreasing:

```lean
def ReducibleBy
    {σ S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [DecidableEq σ]
    (G : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S))
    (p q : MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S) : Prop := ...

def NormalForm
    {σ S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [DecidableEq σ]
    (G : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S))
    (p : MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ q, ReducibleBy G p q
```

For termination, define a measure into a well-founded order. A robust first choice is the cardinality-plus-embedding of support signatures into a finite ambient type when `[Fintype σ]`:

```lean
def pairMeasure
    {σ S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [DecidableEq σ] [Fintype σ]
    (p : MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S) : ℕ := ...
```

or better, a multiset/finset measure if you can access a ready-made well-founded order:

```lean
def pairSupportMeasure
    {σ S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [DecidableEq σ]
    (p : MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S) : Finset (σ →₀ ℕ) := ...
```

with lemmas showing strict decrease under reduction.

### Intermediate theorem package

You should aim to prove the following sequence.

#### 1. Injective elimination via range equivalence

```lean
theorem rename_injective_equiv_range
    {S σ τ : Type*} [CommSemiring S]
    [DecidableEq σ] [DecidableEq τ]
    (ι : τ ↪ σ) :
    ∃ e : MvPolynomial τ S ≃+* renameSubsemiring (S := S) ι, True
```

This is the structural bridge from variable embeddings to elimination along a subsemiring generated by the image variables.

Then:

```lean
theorem elimination_fg_of_embedding
    {S σ τ : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [IsIdempotentElem S (+)]
    [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] [Fintype τ] [DecidableEq τ]
    (ι : τ ↪ σ)
    (C : Con (MvPolynomial σ S)) :
    C.FinitelyGenerated →
    (C.comap (MvPolynomial.rename ι)).FinitelyGenerated
```

#### 2. Finite generation of intersection with an embedded variable subsemiring

If the API naturally prefers a restriction theorem, prove:

```lean
theorem restrict_fg_of_embedding
    {S σ τ : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [IsIdempotentElem S (+)]
    [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] [Fintype τ] [DecidableEq τ]
    (ι : τ ↪ σ)
    (C : Con (MvPolynomial σ S)) :
    C.FinitelyGenerated →
    (C.restrict (renameSubsemiring (S := S) ι)).FinitelyGenerated
```

This is the exact Noetherian input needed for every later completion argument.

#### 3. Well-foundedness of support reduction

For your reduction relation, prove a strict descent theorem:

```lean
theorem reduce_decreases_measure
    {σ S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [DecidableEq σ] [Fintype σ]
    (G : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S))
    {p q : MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S} :
    ReducibleBy G p q →
    pairMeasure q < pairMeasure p
```

Then derive termination:

```lean
theorem reduction_wellFounded
    {σ S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [DecidableEq σ] [Fintype σ]
    (G : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S)) :
    WellFounded (ReducibleBy G)
```

If strict measure decrease is too coarse, use `InvImage` of a well-founded relation on finite support signatures.

#### 4. Existence of normal forms

```lean
theorem exists_normalForm
    {σ S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [DecidableEq σ] [Fintype σ]
    (G : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S))
    (p : MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S) :
    ∃ q, ReflTransGen (ReducibleBy G) p q ∧ NormalForm G q
```

This theorem is already a major algorithmic milestone: it turns finite generating data into a terminating rewrite system candidate.

#### 5. Buchberger-style completion for congruence pairs

Define an `SPair` or critical-pair constructor on polynomial pairs, at least support-theoretically:

```lean
def SPair
    {σ S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [DecidableEq σ]
    (p q : MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S) :
    MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S := ...
```

Then prove a finite completion theorem in the weakest viable form:

```lean
theorem exists_finite_completed_basis
    {S σ : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [IsIdempotentElem S (+)]
    [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ]
    (C : Con (MvPolynomial σ S)) :
    C.FinitelyGenerated →
    ∃ G : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S),
      GeneratesCongruence G C ∧
      CompletedBasis G
```

Here `GeneratesCongruence G C` and `CompletedBasis G` are new definitions you should introduce. `CompletedBasis G` should assert enough closure of critical pairs to imply that reduction to normal form decides congruence membership, but it need not initially be the strongest possible analogue of classical Buchberger.

Finally extract the algorithmic corollary:

```lean
theorem congruence_mem_iff_normalForm_eq
    {S σ : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [IsIdempotentElem S (+)]
    [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ]
    {C : Con (MvPolynomial σ S)}
    {G : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S)} :
    GeneratesCongruence G C →
    CompletedBasis G →
    ∀ p q : MvPolynomial σ S,
      C p q ↔
      normalForm G (p, q) = normalForm G (q, q)
```

If equality to a canonical representative is awkward, use “their reduced pair normalizes to a diagonal pair” or another equivalent criterion.

### Proof strategy: concrete architecture

#### Strategy A: Reduce injective elimination to the known elimination theorem through a subtype/range equivalence
This is the most promising route.

1. Construct the variable-image subsemiring inside `MvPolynomial σ S` generated by variables `X (ι i)`.
2. Show `MvPolynomial.rename ι : MvPolynomial τ S →+* MvPolynomial σ S` lands in this subsemiring and induces a semiring equivalence onto it.
3. Transport the congruence `C` to a congruence on that subsemiring; identify its finite generation with finite generation of the comap along `rename ι`.
4. Apply the existing `elimination_fg` theorem to the subsemiring/range formulation already in the catalog.
5. Push finite generation back across the equivalence.

Key lemmas likely needed:
- injectivity of `MvPolynomial.rename ι` for embeddings;
- characterization of the support of renamed polynomials;
- extensionality on image variables;
- transport of `FinitelyGenerated` across semiring equivalences.

#### Strategy B: Prove finite generation directly by pulling back a finite generating family
Use only if Strategy A hits API obstacles.

1. Start from a finite generating set `T` for `C`.
2. For each generator pair `(f,g)` in `T`, eliminate variables outside `range ι` using the existing elimination infrastructure.
3. Show every relation in the comap congruence is generated by finitely many such eliminated pairs.
4. Use finite support of polynomials and finiteness of the variable types to close the construction.

This is conceptually direct, but likely much more painful in Lean because it requires explicit manipulation of generated congruences.

#### Strategy C: For completion, prove a Dickson-style termination theorem on support signatures
Most promising for the normalization side.

1. Define support signatures in `(σ →₀ ℕ)` and order them by divisibility / componentwise ≤.
2. Invoke Dickson’s lemma on finitely many variables to obtain a well-quasi-order on monomials.
3. Lift this to finite unions/signatures for polynomial pairs.
4. Show every nontrivial reduction strictly decreases the chosen signature.
5. Deduce that every completion sequence terminates once injective elimination prevents new independent variables from proliferating.

If a full WQO on finite sets is awkward, use a simpler natural-number measure first to establish existence of normal forms, then state the stronger WQO-based completion theorem as a conjecture with precise type.

### Recommended concrete proof steps

1. **Build the range model of embedded variables.**
   Prove that the image of `MvPolynomial.rename ι` is exactly the subsemiring of polynomials whose monomial support is contained in exponents on `range ι`. This is the hidden structural lemma behind injective elimination.

2. **Transport finite generation across equivalence.**
   Introduce a general lemma:
   ```lean
   theorem finitelyGenerated_congruence_map_iff
       {R A B : Type*} [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
       (e : A ≃+* B) (C : Con A) :
       C.FinitelyGenerated ↔ (C.map e.toMonoidHom).FinitelyGenerated
   ```
   or the variant compatible with your congruence API. This lemma will pay for itself repeatedly.

3. **Define reduction in a support-monotone way.**
   Don’t overcommit to a coefficient-sensitive notion. In idempotent semirings, support containment is already a natural reduction invariant. Define reduction so that replacing a pair by a generator-translated pair strictly shrinks support.

4. **Prove well-foundedness via a measure.**
   If `Finset (σ →₀ ℕ)` is too hard to order directly, use:
   - cardinality of support union;
   - then sum of total degrees;
   - then lexicographic combination.
   This often suffices for a first formal Buchberger theorem.

5. **Package completion abstractly.**
   Define `CompletedBasis G` by the property that every critical pair reduces to a normal form lying on the diagonal congruence. Then prove that from finite generation and termination one can enlarge any finite generating set to such a `G`.

### If full Buchberger completion is too ambitious

Prove the strongest infrastructure theorem you can fully certify:

```lean
theorem exists_finite_normalizing_basis
    {S σ : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [IsIdempotentElem S (+)]
    [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ]
    (C : Con (MvPolynomial σ S)) :
    C.FinitelyGenerated →
    ∃ G : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S),
      GeneratesCongruence G C ∧
      (∀ p, ∃ q, ReflTransGen (ReducibleBy G) p q ∧ NormalForm G q)
```

This is already a genuine breakthrough: a terminating normalization system for finitely generated idempotent congruences.

If confluence or canonical uniqueness remains open, state it precisely as a conjecture:

```lean
conjecture normalForm_unique_of_completedBasis
    {S σ : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [IsIdempotentElem S (+)]
    [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ]
    {G : Finset (MvPolynomial σ S × MvPolynomial σ S)} :
    CompletedBasis G →
    ∀ p q₁ q₂,
      ReflTransGen (ReducibleBy G) p q₁ →
      ReflTransGen (ReducibleBy G) p q₂ →
      NormalForm G q₁ →
      NormalForm G q₂ →
      q₁ = q₂
```

### Why this matters

This is the idempotent-semiring analogue of the passage from Hilbert basis to elimination theory to Gröbner bases. The injective elimination theorem is the Noetherian spine: it says variable restriction preserves finite describability, exactly what is needed to make local rewrite data global and algorithmic. The normalization/completion layer then turns finite generation from a static existence theorem into a computational engine.

If formalized cleanly, this opens at least three new directions immediately:

1. **Tropical computational algebra.** Congruences over idempotent semirings are the algebraic core of tropical varieties; a canonical finite basis gives an actual decision procedure for tropical polynomial equivalence modulo finitely generated relations.

2. **Automated reasoning in max-plus/min-plus systems.** Normal forms for congruence pairs become symbolic simplifiers for optimization, control, and discrete event systems.

3. **A new Gröbner theory beyond rings.** Classical Buchberger relies on subtraction; this program replaces it by support geometry and congruence pairs. That is not an incremental variant — it is a different algebraic civilization.

Implement the theorem package in Lean with the injective elimination theorem fully proved if at all possible. If the full completion theorem is not reachable in one pass, prioritize:

1. `elimination_fg_of_embedding`,

5. the strongest finite-basis completion statement you can certify.

- a Dickson-lemma-based monomial divisibility order replacing coarse support cardinality;
- extraction of a certified congruence-membership algorithm;
- tropical variety applications of canonical congruence bases;
- extension from finite variable sets to finitely supported infinite-variable elimination.

## YOUR ASSIGNMENT: Functorial resultant and projection reconstruction for idempotent semiring congruences

Work in a commutative idempotent semiring `S`, with polynomial variables split as `Option σ`, where `none` is the eliminated variable and `some i` are the retained variables. The goal is to build a genuinely new elimination mechanism for congruences on `MvPolynomial`, parallel to classical resultant elimination but adapted to semiring congruences rather than ideals.

This is not just a technical variant of existing elimination. If successful, it creates an algorithmic projection calculus for tropical/idempotent algebra: a way to turn generators involving an eliminated variable into explicit projected congruence relations on the remaining variables. That is a bridge from abstract finite generation to constructive elimination, and it is exactly the kind of infrastructure needed for tropical Nullstellensatz-style certification, congruence Gröbner analogues, and effective model projection in idempotent algebraic geometry.

### Core definitions to implement

Use the retained-variable ring
```lean
abbrev R (S : Type*) (σ : Type*) [CommSemiring S] := MvPolynomial σ S
abbrev P (S : Type*) (σ : Type*) [CommSemiring S] := MvPolynomial (Option σ) S
```

Interpret a polynomial in `P S σ` as a univariate polynomial in the distinguished variable `none` with coefficients in `R S σ`.

The key first definition should be a coefficient extractor:
```lean
noncomputable def coeffNone
    {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] {σ : Type*}
    (n : ℕ) : P S σ →+ R S σ
```
with intended behavior
```lean
coeffNone n f =
  ∑ d in f.support.filter (fun m => m none = n),
    monomial (fun i => m (some i)) (f.coeff m)
```
or an equivalent finitely supported formulation.

Then prove the structural lemmas:
```lean
theorem coeffNone_add
    {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] {σ : Type*} (n : ℕ) (f g : P S σ) :
    coeffNone n (f + g) = coeffNone n f + coeffNone n g

theorem coeffNone_monomial_none
    {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] {σ : Type*} (n k : ℕ) (a : R S σ) :
    coeffNone n ((X (none : Option σ))^k * rename Option.some a)
      = if n = k then a else 0
```
and especially finite support / degree cutoff lemmas:
```lean
theorem coeffNone_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt
    {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] {σ : Type*} (f : P S σ) {n : ℕ} :
    natTrailingDegree? -- or your own bounded-support notion
```
If Mathlib has no suitable `natDegree` for `MvPolynomial (Option σ)`, define a custom “degree in the distinguished variable”:
```lean

    {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] {σ : Type*} (f : P S σ) : ℕ
```
as the maximum exponent of `none` on the support, with theorem
```lean
theorem coeffNone_eq_zero_of_noneDegree_lt
    {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] {σ : Type*} (f : P S σ) {n : ℕ}

```

```lean
structure PolyPair (S : Type*) (σ : Type*) [CommSemiring S] where
  lhs : P S σ
```

```lean

    {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] {σ : Type*} :
    R S σ →+* P S σ :=
  rename Option.some

def eliminationCong
    {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] {σ : Type*}
    (C : Con P S σ) : Con (R S σ) :=
  C.comap liftSome
```
Replace `Con` by the actual Mathlib congruence type in the existing infrastructure, e.g. `Setoid`, `SemiringCon`, or the catalog’s congruence object.

```lean
    {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] {σ : Type*}

    eliminationCong C f g ↔ C (liftSome f) (liftSome g)
```

```lean
structure PrimeNucleus (R : Type u) [Semiring R] [ClosureLike R] where
  val : Nucleus R
  ne_top : val ≠ ⊤

    ∀ ⦃I J : Nucleus R⦄, I ⊓ J ≤ val → I ≤ val ∨ J ≤ val
```

```lean
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Lattice
import Mathlib.Order.CompleteLattice
import Mathlib.Order.Zorn
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Basic

open Set

structure FiniteClosureSystem (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] where
  cl : Set α → Set α
  mono_cl : Monotone cl
  extensive : ∀ s, s ⊆ cl s
  idempotent : ∀ s, cl (cl s) = cl s
  cl_empty : cl ∅ = ∅
  cl_union : ∀ s t, cl (s ∪ t) = cl (cl s ∪ cl t)
```

Then define closed theories and primality at the level of closed sets:

```lean
structure Theory (C : FiniteClosureSystem α) where
  carrier : Set α
  is_closed : C.cl carrier = carrier

instance (C : FiniteClosureSystem α) : SetLike (Theory C) where
  coe T := T.carrier
  coe_injective' := by
    intro A B h; cases A; cases B; cases h; rfl

def Theory.le (K P : Theory C) : Prop := (K : Set α) ⊆ (P : Set α)

instance (C : FiniteClosureSystem α) : LE (Theory C) := ⟨Theory.le⟩

def theoryJoin (C : FiniteClosureSystem α) (K L : Theory C) : Theory C :=
  ⟨C.cl ((K : Set α) ∪ (L : Set α)), C.idempotent _⟩

def IsPrimeTheory (C : FiniteClosureSystem α) (P : Theory C) : Prop :=
  ∀ K L : Theory C, theoryJoin C K L ≤ P → K ≤ P ∨ L ≤ P
```

